as_written_in_papers.quote: we identified a pathogenic hemizygous 3' splice site mutation, c.741+2T>C, in intron 5 of the LAMP2 gene (Figure 1C)
a novel splice-altering mutation (LAMP2 c.741+2T>C) in 3'-splice site of exon 5

cases.statement: One family: a hemizygous male proband (19) and his heterozygous mother (42), both with cardiac-only findings.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: HCM (IVS 20 mm, LVEF 50%); paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia; intraventricular block; normal cognition, muscle strength, EMG and CK

quotes.quote: A 19-year-old normally developing man was referred to our hospital with a 3-month history of paroxysmal palpitations and dyspnea after exercise.

The echocardiography revealed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in left ventricular end-diastolic dimension (50 mm), left atrium (34 mm), interventricular septum end-diastolic thickness (20 mm), and posterior wall end-diastolic thickness (18 mm), with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 50%.
The 12-lead ECG and 24 h Holter ECG monitoring of the patient revealed paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia and intraventricular block (Figure 1A).
The patient had normal bilateral muscle strength in the physical examination. The electromyography was normal.
In laboratory tests, his NT-proBNP, TnI, CK, lactic acid, liver and kidney function, levels of serum electrolytes, blood glucose, and lipids were all in the normal range.

people.label: mother of patient
people.key_phenotypes: paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia on Holter; occasional palpitation after exercise; normal echocardiogram; normal blood tests

quotes.quote: The 42-year-old mother of the patient had no other clinical manifestation besides occasional palpitation after exercise.
The mother was also diagnosed with paroxysmal ventricular tachycardia by 24 h Holter ECG monitoring, however, the echocardiography did not show obvious anomalies.
The mutation was also identified in the mother (heterozygous)

phenotype_specificity.statement: A 142-gene cardiomyopathy and channelopathy panel with CNV analysis found no other candidate variants. The authors call the cardiac-only presentation (no myopathy, no intellectual disability) different from typical Danon disease. No biopsy is reported.

quotes.quote: a “cardiomyopathy-ion channelopathy” panel, including 142 causal and candidate genes, was designed
No other potential pathogenic variants or CNVs were filtered in the coding regions and flanking regulated regions of known hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or ion channelopathy-related genes.

The main symptoms of the two patients in the pedigree were based on arrhythmia and were lack of symptoms associated with skeletal myopathy and mental retardation, which is quite different from typical reported DD clinical features (1).

segregation.statement: The affected hemizygous son and his heterozygous mother (paroxysmal VT) carry the variant. Other relatives, described as clinically unremarkable, do not carry it; the text does not give their number (the father is among them, as his DNA was used for the minigene). The authors call this co-segregation.

quotes.quote: The LAMP2 c.741+2T>C mutation was identified in the proband (hemizygous) and his mother (heterozygous) but was absent in other healthy relatives, which implied a co-segregation in the pedigree (Figure 1B).
The rest of his relatives did not show obvious anomalies during physical or laboratory examinations (Figure 1B).
In the follow-up of 2 years, all the family members did not develop neurological or muscular symptoms.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the proband: inherited from his heterozygous mother. Her parents' testing is not reported.

quotes.quote: The mutation was also identified in the mother (heterozygous) but was not identified in the rest relatives or the extra 800 unrelated Chinese healthy controls (Figure 1).

functional.statement: Minigene construct (exon 5 with flanking intron, vector pET01) in HEK293 cells, wild-type vs mutant, with a blank control, in triplicate. RT-PCR showed a slightly larger mutant product; Sanger sequencing of the cDNA showed 6 bp of intron 5 retained, which creates a stop codon. No patient RNA or protein was studied.

quotes.quote: We designed a pair of minigene plasmids (wild-type and mutant) for the LAMP2 gene 3' -splice site mutation (c.741+2T>C).
Human embryonic kidney 293 cells were transfected in triplicates and total RNA was extracted after 48 h using a RNeasy Mini kit (Qiagen, Germany).
The results showed that the mutation disrupted the splice donor site (GT) in intron 5.
We compared the RT–PCR products of wild-type and mutant mRNA by electrophoresis and found the mutant cDNA was a little larger than the wild-type cDNA (Figure 2B).
By Sanger sequencing, we identified a 6-bp insertion at the junction of exons 5 and 6 in the mutant cDNA.
Con, represents blank control without any cDNA.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Change at the +2 position of the intron 5 splice donor (p.? from HGVS). In the minigene assay it led to a 6-nt retention containing an in-frame stop. The authors predict a protein truncated to 248 residues that lacks the transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains. They note that the adjacent c.741+1G>A gave the same 6-bp retention in patient muscle.

quotes.quote: The inserted sequence encoded an in-frame stop codon, which predicted a premature termination of the nascent polypeptide (Figure 2C).
The mutation truncated the LAMP2 protein to 248-amino-acid residues, which lacks the transmembrane domain and the cytoplasmic domain, therefore, fail to function properly (Figure 3).
The reported mutation was demonstrated to cause the same 6-bp mRNA preservation and protein-truncating consequences by using skeletal muscle biopsy samples of the patients with DD (2).

computational_predictions.statement: The authors report evolutionary conservation of the site and an AlphaFold model of the truncated protein. No splice-predictor scores are reported.

quotes.quote: Furthermore, the mutation was in an evolutionary highly conserved region across multiple species (Figure 1C).
The mutant LAMP2 protein was predicted to have a conformational change, lacks the important transmembrane domain, and subsequent protein destabilization.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Absent from 800 unrelated Chinese healthy controls and from ExAC, as the paper states.

quotes.quote: The mutation was neither in the Exome Aggregation Consortium (ExAC; http://exac.broadinstitute.org/) database, nor the extra 800 healthy controls.
The mutation was absent in all public databases.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it pathogenic according to the ACMG guideline. No criteria codes are given.

quotes.quote: we identified a pathogenic hemizygous 3' splice site mutation, c.741+2T>C, in intron 5 of the LAMP2 gene (Figure 1C), according to the ACMG guideline (11).
We describe a specific family with a novel pathogenic splice-altering mutation in the LAMP2 gene (c.741+2T>C)

concerns: Terminology contradiction in the paper: c.741+2T>C is called a "3' splice site" mutation throughout, yet the paper also says it disrupts the splice donor (GT) of intron 5. A +2 intronic position is the donor (5') site of the intron, or the 3' end of exon 5.
The minigene result is described as an insertion 'at the junction of exons 5 and 6' and also as 'between exon 5 and exon SA'. The construct holds only exon 5; SA is the vector exon.

The minigene template was amplified 'from the genomic DNA of the patient or his father'. The father would supply the wild-type allele. The figure legend's genotype notation is unusual ('–/– represents hemizygous', '+/+ represents a wild type').
The 248-residue truncation is inferred from the minigene cDNA sequence and modelling. No patient transcript or protein was examined.
No transcript is stated. The cardiac-only phenotype is described by the authors as atypical.
notes_for_panel: Maternally inherited canonical-donor change, with a construct-based splicing assay (6-nt retention, in-frame stop), absence from 800 controls and a mother-son pair with arrhythmia. No other relative carries it. The family has no extracardiac features.
